key_insight: Tokeniser construction can be cast as a convex optimisation problem: by relaxing the combinatorial vocabulary selection into a linear program and solving it globally (ConvexTok), you get better vocabularies than greedy methods like BPE/Unigram.
problem_solved: Current subword tokenisers use greedy, local decisions that don't optimize the vocabulary as a whole, producing suboptimal token sets and less-efficient encodings (higher bits-per-byte).
method: Formulate tokeniser/vocabulary selection as a linear program (convex relaxation of the combinatorial selection problem).
Solve the relaxed problem using convex optimisation tools to obtain a globally-informed continuous solution.
Recover a discrete vocabulary from the continuous solution (rounding/pruning) to produce the final tokeniser, yielding the ConvexTok algorithm.
impact: ConvexTok provides a principled, global alternative to greedy tokenisation that consistently improves intrinsic token metrics and reduces bits-per-byte, helping practitioners build more compact and efficient token vocabularies for training and deployment.
visual_elements: Side-by-side flowchart: Greedy tokeniser (local splits) vs ConvexTok (LP formulation → convex solver → discrete vocabulary).
Bar chart showing intrinsic tokenisation metrics and bits-per-byte (BpB) comparison: BPE / Unigram / ConvexTok.
Diagram illustrating the convex relaxation: discrete selection space vs relaxed continuous polytope and the solver finding a global optimum.
Before/after tokenisation examples on a short text snippet to show qualitative differences in token splits and token counts.
paper_authors: Jan Tempus, Philip Whittington, Craig W. Schmidt, Dennis Komm, Tiago Pimentel
